newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle closes mostly down on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle closes mostly down on USDA report.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mostly lower with nearbys weakened by a bearish cattle-on-feed report issued Friday by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

The report put marketings during June in large lots in the leading seven states at a lower than expected 102 percent of a year ago, raising concerns that high replacement costs were prompting feedlots to hold cattle for longer and market them at heavier weights.
Floor sources said funds were early sellers of August with late selling interest scattered. LIT was a featured buyer of August.
Refco and R.J. O'Brien were noted sellers of October with Cargill Investor Services on the buy-side, they added.
August live cattle closed 0.500 cent lower at 66.050 cents a lb with other months down 0.225 cent to up 0.150 cent.
Feeder cattle futures closed mixed with the constructive impact of lower CBOT corn prices offset by sentiment the market appears overbought after its recent run-up.
August rose early to a contract high of 83.400 cents, the highest level for the nearby month since January 1994, but slipped back to close down 0.025 cent a lb at 82.750 cents.
Other months ended up 0.225 cent to off 0.225 cent.
Dealers noted the latest CME feeder index, for July 18, was up $0.21 at $82.14 per cwt, the highest level since March 16, 1994.
In live cattle options there was commercial selling of October calls with strike prices of 70 and 71 cents while light selling of August calls with a strike price of 68 cents was also noted.
Volatility was down around 0.50 to 1.00 percent.
